title: Concept Drills — Rate of Heat Flow (Class 11 Physics)
subject: physics

questions.concept: Conduction needs a medium, no bulk flow
questions.question: How does heat travel along a metal spoon in hot tea without the metal itself moving?
questions.solution: By CONDUCTION: energetic particles at the hot end vibrate more violently and pass energy to neighbours through interactions — plus free electrons drift and carry energy in metals. There is no bulk transport of matter (that would be convection); the spoon's atoms stay in place while energy flows through them.

questions.question: Why are cooking pots metal with wooden or plastic handles? Name the property involved and the physical reason for the difference.
questions.solution: Thermal conductivity k: metals have free electrons that transport energy efficiently (k ~ 100–400 W/m·K); wood/plastic lack free carriers and energy must crawl through lattice vibrations (k ~ 0.1). The pot body must conduct (spread heat), the handle must not (protect the hand) — the same property, engineered in opposite directions.

questions.question: State the factors that determine the rate of heat conduction through a window pane, and explain why double glazing works.
questions.solution: dQ/dt = kA(θ₁−θ₂)/d — proportional to conductivity k and area A and temperature difference, inversely to thickness d. Double glazing traps a layer of AIR (k ≈ 0.026, ~10⁴ times worse than glass) between panes, effectively multiplying d with a poor conductor — heat flow collapses. Trapped air, not extra glass, does the insulating.

questions.question: Why does heating water from BELOW circulate it, but heating from above leaves it still?
questions.solution: Convection needs density differences: heated bottom water expands, becomes less dense, rises; cooler water sinks to replace it — a convection current. Heated from above, the warm (less dense) layer is already on top and no circulation can start. Gravity acting on density differences is the engine of convection.

questions.question: How does the Sun's heat reach Earth through empty space, and what makes a surface a good absorber of this heat?
questions.solution: By RADIATION — electromagnetic waves (mainly infrared) that need no medium. Absorption/emission depend on surface nature: black, rough surfaces absorb and emit best; white, polished surfaces reflect (poor absorbers AND poor emitters). That is why vacuum flasks silver their walls — cutting radiation loss.
